quarterly_data.signal: MaxLinear's 10-Q: inventory purchase obligations were $272,967 thousand as of September 30, 2026 ($88,690 thousand due in the remaining three months of 2026 and $184,277 thousand in 2027). Working-capital investment reduced nine-month operating cash flow by approximately $137.6 million, 'primarily due to prepayments for wafers and purchases of inventory supporting rising demand for certain data center products'; inventory was $113,722 thousand (work-in-process $79,013 thousand) versus $78,104 thousand at December 31, 2025, and planned capital expenditures are expected to increase to support production needs.
quarterly_data.figure: inventory purchase obligations $272,967 thousand ($184,277 thousand in 2027); approximately $137.6 million working-capital use (wafer prepayments, inventory)

quarterly_data.signal: 10-Q customer and shipment mix: no customer accounted for 10% or more of net revenue in the quarter ended September 30, 2026 (Customer A 18% and Customer B 11% a year earlier); Customer A was 10% of nine-month 2026 revenue (17% a year earlier). Products shipped to Hong Kong were 52% of Q3 net revenue, mainland China 12% and Vietnam 12%; Asia 89%. Infrastructure was 57% of Q3 net revenue (32% a year earlier) and $272,737 thousand for the nine months (+168%), driven by higher shipments of optical, products for data center applications, high-performance analog, and wireless backhaul and access products; broadband fell on lower cable data shipments 'driven by a customer's transition to a new standard'.
quarterly_data.figure: no 10% customer in Q3 2026; Customer A 10% (9M 2026); Hong Kong 52%, mainland China 12%, Vietnam 12%; infrastructure 57% of revenue

quarterly_data.signal: 10-Q legal proceedings on the terminated Silicon Motion merger: Silicon Motion's arbitration at the Singapore International Arbitration Centre (filed October 5, 2023) seeks the termination fee, additional damages, fees and costs; on May 14, 2026 the HBK Plaintiffs (HBK Master Fund L.P. and HBK Merger Strategies Master Fund L.P.) filed a complaint in the Superior Court of California, County of San Diego, alleging common law and statutory fraud, negligent misrepresentation and interference claims and seeking compensatory and punitive damages. MaxLinear says it properly terminated the merger agreement and intends to vigorously defend these claims.
